previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent cellulitis, venous stasis ulcers, chronic pancreatitis, and asthma was admitted for worsening cellulitis of the left lower leg that failed outpatient treatment with minocycline. She presented with spreading erythema, fever, chills, and burning pain, and was started on IV vancomycin in the emergency department. During her two-day hospitalization, her infection improved clinically and her white blood cell count normalized. A chest X-ray showed no acute findings despite her cough and sputum, consistent with an upper respiratory infection. A lower extremity ultrasound ruled out DVT. She was discharged on oral minocycline for a 10-day course and instructed to follow up with her primary care provider for ongoing management and blood culture results.

# Cellulitis: Persistent despite greater than 2 weeks of oral 
antibiotics. On exam she has a single draining open wound over 
the left lateral malleolis. In the setting of failed treatment 
of this cellulitis, multiple past episodes lower extremity 
cellulitis, purulence on physical exam, and a history of MRSA, 
the decision was made to treat with IV vancomycin for empiric 
coverage of MRSA. Wound culture results returned showing MSSA, 
and she was converted to clindamycin, for a total course of 10 
days. 

# Hives: She developed hives on her upper and lower extremities. 
There was no correlation between the onset of antibiotics and 
the development of hives. She reports multiple prior episodes of 
spontaneous hives occurring on past hospitalization, and 
referred to them as her ""hospital hives"". She was treated 
symptomatically with benadryl and was given bleech-free sheets.

# GERD: Her home medication was not on formulary, so we give her
